- the multidimensional methods are generally more efficient than the unidimensional methods for QTL mapping, - the use of synthetic variables is a good compromise to combine the advantages of both unidimensional and multivariate approaches, - the use is recommended of the synthetic variable method to select the best characters to be analyzed by the multivariate methods, - the use can be recommended of the multivariate method to select the chromosomal regions to be analyzed by unidimensional methods, - the multivariate methods
the multidimensionnal methods developed in this work are more powerful and precise to detect QTL affecting correlated characters than the unidimensional methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods for QTL mapping in livestock species, based on correlated traits.
the detection of quantitative trait loci (QTL), that is, genomic regions affecting quantitative traits.
the development of methods for mapping QTL affecting quantitative traits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(1) multivariate QTL detection methods, based on the analysis of correlated phenotypes and markers, are very powerful and accurate, (2) univariate methods based on the analysis on a synthetic variable (linear combination of the traits) are also powerful, but are less accurate, and (3) the use of univariate methods is recommended when the number of traits is large.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed methods to detect QTL affecting correlated traits and/or traits linked, in livestock populations.
we have developed methods to map QTL for correlated quantitative traits.
we have developed and tested methods for mapping QTL affecting correlated traits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of multivariate methods is a promising strategy for the detection of QTL.
the use of a synthetic variable can improve the power and accuracy of QTL mapping, especially in the case of a large number of QTL and correlated phenotypes.
, in most situations, the use of multivariate methods to analyze QTL data is not only feasible but also advantageous.
